story.title: France Accuses Iran of Major Cyberattacks on Supermarket Refrigerators
story.summary: France has accused Iran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating significant cyberattacks on supermarket refrigerators last month, resulting in the spoilage of millions of dollars' worth of food. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot described the attacks as unprecedented and announced plans for European sanctions against those responsible. The cyberattacks involved taking control of refrigeration systems at around 700 retail locations, raising temperatures during the night.

explore_lenses.label: What changed on the ground?
explore_lenses.title: Sabotage affected more than retail fridges
explore_lenses.summary: French authorities say the October 11-12 intrusion altered industrial refrigeration settings at roughly 700 retail sites, causing food losses and some fires. The same investigation also identified other food-sector and small hydroelectric targets.

claims.text: France’s Foreign Ministry said the campaign hit refrigeration controllers at more than 700 French retail locations, causing major material damage, fires and food losses estimated in the tens of millions of euros.

ANSSI said compromised equipment had its defrost settings raised to high temperatures; it recorded at least 15 fire starts and said victims also included small butcher shops, an abattoir and cooperative food plants.
ANSSI said the campaign also targeted Schneider Electric equipment at small French hydroelectric installations, though it described the effects there as limited.

ANSSI said the campaign also targeted Schneider Electric equipment at small French hydroelectric installations, though it described the effects there as limited.

explore_lenses.label: How did France link the attack to Iran?
explore_lenses.title: Attribution rests on a multi-agency technical case
explore_lenses.summary: France attributes the sabotage to Shahid Kaveh, which it describes as an IRGC-linked offensive cyber unit. Officials present the refrigerator operation as part of a longer pattern of Iran-linked activity against French interests rather than an isolated incident.

claims.text: The French cyber-crisis coordination body (C4) said it attributed the destructive actions to Shahid Kaveh based on infrastructure characteristics, signing tools, amplification by a propaganda outlet linked to the unit, and Persian-language traces in attack infrastructure.
France’s CERT-FR says C4 comprises ANSSI, COMCYBER, the DGA, DGSE and DGSI, and says the refrigeration attack was an unprecedented French-targeted sabotage operation in scale and aggressiveness.

French authorities say IRGC-linked cyber activity against French interests has been observed since at least 2020, citing attacks connected to Charlie Hebdo in 2023 and an attempted compromise of a French digital-signage operator before the 2024 Paris Olympics.

explore_lenses.label: What are the next confirmed steps?
explore_lenses.title: Diplomatic, EU and criminal responses begin
explore_lenses.summary: France has announced diplomatic and legal steps and intends to seek additional EU listings. A new sanctions package is a proposal, not yet a confirmed EU decision as of November 9.

claims.text: France said it would summon Iran’s ambassador and propose new EU sanctions against Iranian individuals and entities involved in this attack and other malicious cyber activity.
ANSSI said the Paris prosecutor’s office opened a judicial investigation and sought international arrest warrants for several alleged Shahid Kaveh members.

The EU had already designated the IRGC as a terrorist organization on February 19, 2026, under its counterterrorism sanctions regime; that existing designation does not itself confirm the new France-proposed cyber listings.
Forecast: France’s proposed measures would require agreement through the EU’s sanctions process before additional names or entities are formally listed.

story_report.summary: France has accused Iran’s Revolutionary Guards of mounting a cyber-sabotage campaign against refrigeration systems at about 700 retail sites last month. French authorities say attackers raised defrost settings to high temperatures, causing major food spoilage and material damage, with losses estimated in the tens of millions of euros and at least 15 fires recorded. Paris called the operation unprecedented in scale and aggressiveness against French targets, said it would summon Iran’s ambassador, and plans to seek further European Union sanctions.

sections.heading: Food Sector Targets Extended Beyond Retail
sections.body: The reported victims extended beyond large retail locations. France’s cybersecurity agency, ANSSI, said the campaign also affected small butcher shops, an abattoir and cooperative food plants. Separately, it said attackers targeted Schneider Electric equipment at small hydroelectric installations, although the effects at those sites were limited. The available official releases do not name the retailers or provide a complete list of affected organizations.

sections.heading: French Agencies Detail Iran Attribution
sections.body: France’s cyber-crisis coordination body, C4, said it attributed the destructive activity to Shahid Kaveh using infrastructure characteristics, signing tools, promotion by a propaganda outlet linked to the unit, and Persian-language traces in the attack infrastructure. C4 includes ANSSI, COMCYBER, the DGA, DGSE and DGSI, according to CERT-FR. French authorities also say they have observed IRGC-linked cyber activity against French interests since at least 2020, including incidents tied to Charlie Hebdo and an attempted compromise before the Paris Olympics.

sections.heading: France Pursues Sanctions and Criminal Investigation
sections.body: France said it will propose new EU sanctions against Iranian individuals and entities allegedly involved in the attack and other malicious cyber activity. ANSSI said the Paris prosecutor’s office has opened a judicial investigation and sought international arrest warrants for several alleged Shahid Kaveh members. The IRGC was already designated by the EU as a terrorist organization on February 19, 2026, but any additional cyber-related listings would require agreement through the EU sanctions process.

unresolved.text: French releases do not provide a fully disclosed forensic record supporting the attribution, and the official materials consulted included no Iranian response.
Authorities have not identified all affected businesses or supplied an independently audited total for food losses.
France has not publicly named the people or entities it will nominate for EU measures, set a timetable for a decision, or said whether the requested arrest warrants can be executed.

related_stories.summary: Nvidia has launched an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being a spy for China. Reports indicate that Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang may have made him a target of foreign intelligence efforts. Following the announcement of the investigation, Nvidia's stock price experienced a significant drop, and U.S. intelligence officials have raised concerns about the implications of this relationship.

related_stories.title: Impeachment Vote Looms for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Following Massie's Resolution
related_stories.summary: Representative Thomas Massie has introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of engaging in military actions against Iran without congressional authorization. A vote in the House is expected to take place this week, which, if successful, would lead to a Senate trial. Hegseth has expressed confidence regarding the impeachment efforts and plans to defend his record in a news conference.
